decisions.reason: A same-message MODIFY already records the minute Hero V right-arm length increase and preservation of all other geometry.

The existing MODIFY records the length method but omits the client's clarification that endpoint elevation is the mechanical result of a same-line length increase rather than an independently altered terminal.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Kenji,

Thank you again for approaching every round so systematically. Your process has made this much easier, and it truly feels as though we’ve reached the final refinements.

After reviewing these versions, I realized that my use of the word reach unintentionally created ambiguity. What I meant was mechanical rather than artistic: the right arm should become very slightly longer while the existing Option B terminal remains completely unchanged. Length would have communicated the request more accurately.

Because Variation 1 also altered the terminal, I can’t isolate and evaluate the single variable I intended to study. My goal was to compare the original Option B against a version identical in every respect except for a minute increase in right-arm length.

Please approach the next round as follows:

1\. Begin with the original Option B and change only the right arm’s length by a very small amount. Preserve the terminal geometry, taper, point shape, and profile without modification; simply continue the existing arm slightly farther along precisely the same line before it ends. Apply that identical adjustment to the Hero V, second V, and É accent. The horizontal reference line was extremely useful, so please retain it for this comparison.

2\. From the longer Option B version, keep exactly the same length increase and soften only the terminal very slightly. Do not add curvature or create a flourish. The architectural character and straight tip must remain, with only the corners becoming subtly gentler.

3\. Give Option C that same small increase in length while leaving its existing terminal character and overall geometry intact. Carry the treatment consistently across the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

Variations 2 and 3 explored the softer terminal language effectively. The difficulty is that both originated from a Variation 1 terminal that had already changed, making it hard to distinguish the effect of added length from the effect of a redesigned terminal.

We are now evaluating one variable at a time. The architecture, proportions, slope, spacing, and finish all feel locked. The remaining question is whether a slightly longer right arm strengthens the logo and, if so, whether its terminal should stay exactly as it is or become only a touch softer.

Thank you for your thoughtful work and patience with these final nuances. We’re incredibly close.

value_updates.endpoint_adjustment_method: Increase only the right-arm length by continuing the arm slightly farther along precisely the same line.
value_updates.cross_form_application: Apply an identical length adjustment to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.
value_updates.height_relationship: Treat the subtly higher right endpoint as the mechanical result of the minute same-line right-arm length increase, not as an independently redesigned terminal or artistic reach.
value_updates.geometry_invariants: Preserve the Option B terminal geometry, taper, point shape, profile, slope, architecture, proportions, spacing, and finish.

decisions.reason: A same-message MODIFY already records the identical minute length adjustment for the É accent while preserving its Option B terminal geometry.

The source clarifies the terminal rules across all three signature forms, replaces the obsolete no-lengthening constraint, and requires length and terminal softness to be evaluated as isolated variables.

value_updates.shared_terminal_rule: Apply the selected terminal treatment consistently across the Hero V, second V, and É accent while evaluating right-arm length separately from terminal softness.
terminal_adjustment_constraints: For the length-only Option B comparison, preserve the terminal geometry, taper, point shape, and profile unchanged while increasing only the arm length.
For the separately softened variant, soften only the terminal corners slightly without adding curvature or a flourish, and keep the architectural character and straight tip.
value_updates.terminal_treatment: Use the unchanged original Option B terminal for the length-only comparison, with a separate same-length variant that only subtly softens its corners.
value_updates.terminal_refinement_scope: Evaluate minute right-arm length and terminal softness as isolated variables while keeping the wider architecture, proportions, slope, spacing, and finish locked.

decisions.reason: The source keeps spacing and overall composition locked and changes only the signature forms' right-arm length and terminal comparison.
The source does not change the construction, scale, or architectural language of the E, I, or L letterforms.
The source does not identify or change a champagne-gold finish or distribution; its reference to locked finish is incidental to the geometric comparison.
The minute geometric comparison remains consistent with the existing brand-expression goals but does not change those goals.
Changing the signature forms' right-arm length does not alter the decision to use a wordmark-led identity without a separate icon or monogram.
The source concerns design refinement and does not change the production-ready asset-export obligation.
